event_mapping.note: The team format uses event_id 1. Inside PPOST the same wildfire is identified as "EV-2026-014" (every PPOST record has disaster_id = "EV-2026-014"). This mapping is agreed for these sample files only; it is not a database join. Once Earl's disasters table is connected, PPOST will store the real event id.

data.sample_data_note: Synthetic demonstration data for the fictional Clearwater Ridge Wildfire. Generated from the PPOST seed data and the real PPOST rules engine with a sample set of assessment answers. Not live data, not read from Supabase.
data.field_names: snake_case versions of the app's camelCase fields (e.g. priority_id = priorityId, five_w1h = fiveW1H).

dashboard_summary.counting_rule: main_questions_total counts main questions and follow-ups currently shown (follow-ups appear only after their trigger answer). Deeper questions are optional and counted separately. UNANSWERED is never counted as UNKNOWN.

rules.unknown_stays_unknown: An UNKNOWN answer is stored as UNKNOWN and is never converted to YES or NO.
rules.note_required_when: answer is UNKNOWN (what is unknown, why, and who is checking)
rules.problem_created_when: answer equals problem_when (YES unless the question says NO)

unknown_policies.SAFETY: Treat as a potential hazard: precautionary problem (CRITICAL) + safety tactic + verification task.
unknown_policies.VERIFY: No hazard assumed: verification task only.

rules.records_added_only_on_user_action: Generated problems, safety tactics and tasks are added to PPOST as DRAFT only when the user presses 'Add to PPOST as drafts'.

generated_id_patterns.problem: P-<question_id> (YES/NO rule) or P-<question_id>-U (UNKNOWN safety rule); if the question is already linked to an existing problem, that problem is reused

questions.text: Are residents displaced from their homes?
questions.why_we_ask: Displacement drives shelter, income support and psychosocial needs from day one.
questions.problem_title: Displaced residents need shelter and support

questions.text: Do displaced residents include people with medical or mobility needs?
questions.why_we_ask: People who depend on power, medication or mobility aids face the highest risk while displaced.

questions.text: Were responders or residents exposed to heavy smoke, ash or hazardous materials?
questions.why_we_ask: Exposure can cause delayed health effects; responder safety is Priority 1.
questions.problem_title: Health exposure among responders and residents
questions.note: Crew health reports show no smoke-exposure cases this shift (sample note).

questions.text: Were homes destroyed?
questions.why_we_ask: Destroyed homes mean households cannot return and need interim housing.

questions.text: Have damaged (not destroyed) homes been assessed for safe re-entry?
questions.why_we_ask: Re-entering an unassessed home risks injury from structural damage, ash or hazardous materials.
questions.problem_title: Damaged homes not assessed for safe re-entry

questions.text: Are residential areas downslope of severe burn scars at risk of debris flow?
questions.why_we_ask: Burned slopes can produce fast debris flows in the first heavy rains.

questions.text: Is the evacuation route for those homes open?
questions.why_we_ask: If the only route is blocked, residents cannot leave when an alert is issued.

questions.text: Has the municipal water intake or distribution line experienced pressure loss or power loss?
questions.why_we_ask: Pressure loss can let contaminants into drinking water — a public health risk.
questions.note: Utility has not reported pressure readings yet; M. Chen visiting the intake today (sample note).

questions.text: Are there power outages or downed lines in the affected area?
questions.why_we_ask: Downed lines may still be energized; outages affect water, shelters and medical devices.

questions.text: Are key roads or bridges damaged or closed?
questions.why_we_ask: Road access controls how fast crews, supplies and residents can move.

questions.text: Is there a risk of erosion or sediment entering creeks or drinking-water sources?
questions.why_we_ask: Bare soil after a fire washes into waterways, harming fish habitat and water treatment.
questions.problem_title: Erosion and sediment risk to waterways

questions.text: Are there hazardous-material releases (fuel tanks, propane, chemicals, asbestos)?
questions.why_we_ask: Burned structures often release asbestos and fuels that endanger crews and residents.

questions.text: Are local businesses closed because of the event?
questions.why_we_ask: Closures cut household income and the local tax base.

questions.text: Has a disaster funding application already been submitted?
questions.why_we_ask: Funding programs have intake deadlines; knowing the status avoids missing them.
questions.note: Finance has not confirmed whether the DFA application was filed (sample note).

questions.text: Are reception centres or group lodging near capacity?
questions.why_we_ask: Full reception centres mean evacuees may be turned away or sent far from home.
questions.note: Reception centre B reported 92% occupancy at 08:00 (sample note).

questions.text: Are rental or temporary housing options available locally for displaced households?
questions.why_we_ask: If there is nothing to rent locally, interim modular housing or hotel programs are needed.

questions.text: Are telecommunications (cell, internet, 911) disrupted in the affected area?
questions.why_we_ask: Without phones and 911, residents cannot call for help or receive alerts.

questions.text: Is wildlife, fish habitat or a species at risk affected?
questions.why_we_ask: Habitat damage can need permits and specialist restoration work.

questions.text: Are tourism, agriculture or forestry operations affected?
questions.why_we_ask: Primary industries often employ most of a rural community.

questions.text: Can the local government run normal services (staff, offices, records, IT)?
questions.why_we_ask: Recovery depends on a working local government; the Governance sector covers this.

questions.text: Are hospitals, care homes or clinics served by this water system?
questions.why_we_ask: Health facilities cannot operate safely without trusted water.
questions.problem_title: Health facilities on an unverified water supply

questions.text: Is an alternate drinking-water supply (bottled water, tankers) in place?
questions.why_we_ask: Decides whether water distribution must start now.
questions.note: No tanker contract in place yet (sample note).

questions.text: Has the water been sampled and lab-tested since the event?
questions.why_we_ask: Lab results are what allow an advisory to be lifted.

questions.text: Do destroyed homes include rentals, mobile homes or First Nations housing?
questions.why_we_ask: Renters and on-reserve housing follow different programs and funding rules.
questions.problem_title: Displaced renters and specialized housing needs

questions.text: Do most affected owners have home insurance?
questions.why_we_ask: Uninsured households need much more public support to rebuild.

questions.text: Have destroyed lots been screened for asbestos and hazardous materials before clearing?
questions.why_we_ask: Clearing unscreened lots exposes crews and neighbours to asbestos.
questions.problem_title: Destroyed lots not screened for hazardous materials

questions.text: Do displaced residents need language, cultural or Elder supports?
questions.why_we_ask: Supports that fit the community make services usable.

questions.text: Are pets or livestock displaced with their owners?
questions.why_we_ask: People may refuse to evacuate or shelter without their animals.

questions.text: Are any residents dependent on powered medical equipment?
questions.why_we_ask: Oxygen concentrators and similar devices fail within hours without power.
questions.problem_title: Residents on powered medical equipment without power

questions.text: Has the utility given an estimated restoration time?
questions.why_we_ask: The restoration time decides whether temporary power is worth the cost.

questions.text: Is there a detour heavy trucks can use?
questions.why_we_ask: Modular homes, debris trucks and supplies need a heavy-vehicle route.

questions.text: Are schools, clinics or grocery stores cut off by the closure?
questions.why_we_ask: Cut-off essential services make it hard for residents to return.
questions.problem_title: Essential services cut off by road closures

questions.text: Has the release been reported to the provincial environmental emergency line?
questions.why_we_ask: Reporting is required and brings specialist response.
questions.problem_title: Hazmat release not yet reported to authorities

questions.text: Are workers losing income because of the closures?
questions.why_we_ask: Lost wages drive household hardship and out-migration.

questions.text: Do businesses need help applying for grants or loans?
questions.why_we_ask: Small businesses often miss programs because applications are complex.
questions.problem_title: Businesses need help accessing grants or loans
